For claim c1:
The Press Information Bureau (PIB) Fact Check, the Indian government's official fact-checking agency, clarified on September 21, 2026, that the "National Student Laptop Scheme 2026" or any similar program providing free laptops to all students has not been announced by the Government of India. [1] [2] [3] They stated that such claims circulating on social media are fake and part of a scam to collect personal information. [1] [3] [4] While some state-level schemes exist in India, such as Tamil Nadu's Ulagam Ungal Kaiyil and Uttar Pradesh's Swami Vivekananda Yuva Sashaktikaran Yojana (Mission DigiShakti), there is no central government scheme providing free laptops to all students. [5] [2]

For claim c2:
TV9 Bharatvarsh reported on September 14, 2026, that a message circulating on social media claiming a "Students Laptop Scheme 2026" with an application deadline is fake. [4] The Press Information Bureau (PIB) Fact Check also debunked similar claims about a "National Student Laptop Scheme 2026," stating that the Government of India has not announced any such scheme. [1] [2] [3] These messages are identified as fraudulent attempts to gather personal information. [1] [3] [4]

For claim c3:
TV9 Bharatvarsh investigated the viral message about a "Students Laptop Scheme 2026" and found that the website mentioned in the message was blocked, indicating it was part of a fraudulent scheme. [4] The Press Information Bureau (PIB) Fact Check has repeatedly debunked claims about a "PM Free Laptop Scheme" or "National Student Laptop Scheme 2026," confirming these are scams designed to collect personal information. [1] [2] [3] They advise citizens to verify information only through official government sources. [1] [3]
